Under oriented Gr(2,4)=S2xS2 Haar product, two independent polar cosines X,Y produce z=XY+sqrt(1-X²)sqrt(1-Y²)=cos(alpha-beta). Integrating |alpha-beta| gives f(u)=(sin u+(pi-u)cos u)/4, normalized to one. The v=1/2 artanh z substitution yields the convolution of positive integrable h(v)=1/2 sqrt(sin q)(sin q-q cos q) and k(w)=(cosh2w)^-1/2. Differentiating log h twice and the Cusa-Huygens strict trigonometric inequality establishes strict logconcavity; independently symbolically differentiated its stated second-derivative identity. Integral differentiates to Phi’(0)=pi²/16>0; strict logconcavity and decay at infinities force exactly one optimizer t*>0. Negative t refers only to analytic extension, not the same geometric section formula.
